messages:
Elena (finance): Heads-up: vendor invoice INV-4921 includes a $2,400 GPU line we believe should be credited due to mis-tagged project mappings on their billing export. Raised to vendor support.
VendorBot: Support ticket VT-880 opened with CloudVendor: reason=misattributed_skus, requested_action=credit $2400, ETA=48h.
Marco (finops): Can we provisionally hold that $2.4k as pending-credit in the internal ledger so teams aren’t charged prematurely?
Elena (finance): Yes — finance can place a pending hold entry under "vendor_pending_credits". Need approval from eng-ml to confirm they don't claim this cost.
Anya (eng-ml): Confirmed this was not our workload — the instance ids point to a marketing demo. Eng-ml declines claim.
Marco (finops): OK. @Elena please create ledger hold: account=marketing, amount=$2400, note="INV-4921 pending vendor credit". Once vendor confirms credit, finance will apply as contra-charge to invoice and clear the hold.
Elena (finance): Done. Ledger hold created: LH-2026-77. Also added follow-up task FIN-CL-312 to reconcile when VT-880 closes.
VendorBot: VT-880 status=awaiting_vendor_response.
Anya (eng-ml): Thanks — can we add a doc to the runbook for handling vendor misattributions? Small checklist: open ticket, create ledger hold, notify owners, and auto-unassign after 14 days if unresolved.
Elena (finance): Good call. I'll add to FIN runbook and schedule a weekly check for vendor pending credits.
Marco (finops): Approved. Closing note: retro-note=1777777777_vendor_pending_credit.
